publisher_scope_notice: Direct Oxford dictionary observations support inflection, countability and word-sense distinctions ONLY. Oxford topic tags are not independent exact-sense CEFR classification. No independent human bilingual/example approval or audio listening is claimed. All eight frozen entries are unchanged and remain on editorial hold.

records.source_supported_observation: The noun man is countable; its plural is men /men/, not mans. The original singular example is grammatical.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: အရွယ်ရောက်ပြီးသော အမျိုးသား (အများကိန်း men)
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: The man is talking to a teacher.
records.independent_reviewer_question: Confirm the singular adult-male sense and separately teach /mæn/ versus plural /men/ without counting men as a new lemma.

records.original_burmese_meaning: အရွယ်ရောက်ပြီးသော အမျိုးသမီး
records.source_supported_observation: The noun woman is countable; women is the plural and has a different vowel in its British pronunciation. The original singular example is grammatical.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: အရွယ်ရောက်ပြီးသော အမျိုးသမီး (အများကိန်း women)
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: A woman is waiting near the door.
records.independent_reviewer_question: Check British singular /ˈwʊmən/ and plural /ˈwɪmɪn/ with real George/Emma listening if either is used in final audio.

records.original_english_definition: A young person who is not yet an adult.
records.source_supported_observation: Child has the irregular plural children, not childs. The original singular subject and agreement are correct.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: ကလေး (အများကိန်း children)
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: The child is reading a book.
records.independent_reviewer_question: Keep singular child distinct from plural children and require independent A1 exact-sense review.

records.original_english_definition: The part of the body at the end of a leg.
records.source_supported_observation: Body-part foot has plural feet; the separate measurement sense has different use and is not what this A1 card teaches.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: ခြေဖဝါး၊ ခြေထောက်အောက်ပိုင်း (အများကိန်း feet)
records.independent_reviewer_question: Keep body-part sense separate from foot as length unit and do not infer A1 for the measurement sense from the body-part card.

records.original_english_definition: An animal that lives in water and has gills.
records.original_example_sentence: The fish swims in the river.
records.source_supported_observation: Fish is the usual singular/plural animal noun; fishes is used especially for different kinds. Food fish is an uncountable sense. Original sentence teaches an animal.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: ငါး (တိရစ္ဆာန်; အများကိန်းတွင် fish ကို အများအားဖြင့် သုံးသည်)
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: I can see three fish in the pond.
records.independent_reviewer_question: Review whether a plural fish example is understood as plural, and distinguish countable animal from uncountable food.

records.original_english_definition: The thin strands growing on a person's head.
records.source_supported_observation: Hair as all the hair on a head is uncountable; individual hairs can be counted. Original Her hair is long correctly uses the mass noun.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: ဆံပင် (စုစုပေါင်းကို ပြောလျှင် uncountable; တစ်ချောင်းချင်းကို ပြောလျှင် countable)
records.independent_reviewer_question: Ensure Myanmar translation and examples do not incorrectly use hairs for collective head hair.

records.original_english_definition: A farm bird kept for eggs or meat.
records.original_example_sentence: There is a chicken in the garden.
records.source_supported_observation: A chicken is a countable bird; chicken as food is an uncountable meat sense. The original garden example correctly teaches the bird.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: ကြက် (တိရစ္ဆာန်ဆိုလျှင် countable; ကြက်သားဆိုလျှင် uncountable)
records.suggested_example_UNAPPROVED: A chicken is walking in the garden.
records.independent_reviewer_question: Confirm the animal sense and do not silently replace its Myanmar gloss with ကြက်သား, the food sense.

records.original_english_definition: Having the colour between red and yellow.
records.original_burmese_meaning: လိမ္မော်ရောင်ဖြစ်သော
records.source_supported_observation: Orange is a colour adjective in the frozen card; orange as a fruit is a different noun/POS sense. The original The bag is orange is a correct adjective example.
records.suggested_myanmar_UNAPPROVED: လိမ္မော်ရောင်ရှိသော (adjective; လိမ္မော်သီး noun နှင့် ကွဲပြား)
records.independent_reviewer_question: Require independent POS-specific review: the noun fruit evidence is not proof that the adjective card teaches fruit.
